name: aws-serverless
extractedFrom: Newly written — no proven original. No other pack was opened, not even as a format reference (only assets/pack-resource-template.md was used)
policyEngineNote: DynamoDB has no row-level enforcement like RLS. IAM condition keys can restrict some of it but are not a general substitute — the application layer is the only real boundary, and leaving ownership out of the key condition is a data leak in waiting. Move the BaaS axis's 'double defense' statement here and it becomes exactly the opposite guidance

exampleDomain.note: Uses the same example domain as the other packs. From this value L0 issues the vocabulary policy (vocab-task) so the gate blocks divergence

fixesVariantsNote: IaC is pinned to CDK and DynamoDB access to SDK v3's DocumentClient. A project that chose SAM (YAML templates) has an entirely different deployment and permissions section, so assembling this pack hands it the wrong guidance. A variant that goes to a relational DB makes backendType cloud-server, so backend/node-api or aws-container owns it
runtimeNote: These are Lambda runtime versions, not npm dependencies

resources.nav: The Lambda handler shape · API Gateway events and responses · initialization outside the cold start · middleware composition · timeouts and retries · structured logging
Access patterns first · single-table design · PK/SK combinations · choosing a GSI · item shape and version · contrast with relational habits
The DocumentClient singleton · Query vs Scan · ownership in the key condition · conditional writes · pagination (LastEvaluatedKey) · batches and transactions
Zod schemas · parsing the event body, path and query · the environment schema · failing at cold start
Domain error → status code · identifying DynamoDB errors (ConditionalCheckFailed and the rest) · normalizing ZodError · no existence leaks
Composing the CDK stack · least-privilege IAM per function (read/write/batch) · bundling and bundle size · deploy order and irreversible changes
The test harness (invokeHandler) · the arrange step of a handler test · positive/negative pairs · separating the wiring layer from the data layer

seamSlotNotes.api-endpoints: Route↔function mapping and emitting the response envelope. The envelope is a function of the wire contract
seamSlotNotes.auth-boundaries: Cognito token verification · extracting the subject from the claims · roles and scopes. **The auth method is a function of the combination, not of the axis** — a SPA frontend axis means bearer tokens, and a server runtime takes a different shape
seamSlotNotes.complete-example: IaC → table → access pattern → query → handler → test, end to end

clusters.why: The environment schema and the error code table are functions of each other. ZodError → field-error envelope and DynamoDB ConditionalCheckFailed → 409 come out of one table. This is where the AppError shape in requires gets tangled the most
The key design is the query shape. Without a settled PK/SK you cannot use Query, and the GSI choice decides whether an ownership filter is possible at all — one author has to decide them together
The handler lifetime (cold start · where initialization goes · timeouts) and deployment and permissions are one decision. Per-function IAM is a function of what the handler calls

knownGaps.what: The test examples do not run as written
knownGaps.detail: The handler test calls the real `handler` and that chain runs `EnvSchema.safeParse(process.env)` at module load — the vitest process has no `TABLE_NAME` or `AWS_REGION`, so it throws at the import step. Even past that, `getTask` calls the real `ddb.send`. The pack carries no stand-in method (`vi.mock` · seeding · starting DynamoDB Local) (audit A run confirmed: `Test Files 1 failed`)

knownGaps.what: grantTaskAccess does not grant batch or transaction permissions
knownGaps.detail: The pack teaches `TransactWriteCommand`, `BatchWriteCommand` and `BatchGetCommand` as normal patterns, yet the read 2 / write 3 actions of the IAM helper carry no `TransactWriteItems`, `BatchWriteItem`, `BatchGetItem` or `ConditionCheckItem`. Follow the pack and the deploy succeeds while the runtime returns AccessDenied → 500 (audits A and C)

The ordinary UI path of reusing a cursor against a query on a different index takes a DynamoDB `ValidationException` and becomes an `INTERNAL` 500. `data-access.md` admits the risk in prose but there is no mapping (audit A, measured)
